title: Entanglement asymmetry in the gapped XYZ spin-$\frac12$ chain
abstract: The entanglement asymmetry measures how strongly a symmetry is broken inside a subsystem. Analytic results at equilibrium have so far covered free theories and, perturbatively, the critical XXZ chain. We compute the Rényi entanglement asymmetries of a large interval in the gapped, $U(1)$-breaking phase of the interacting XYZ chain. The calculation combines three ingredients. A charged-moment identity, which we prove for fermionic Gaussian and for injective matrix-product ground states, ties the asymmetry to the static susceptibility of the broken charge. A non-conservation sum rule then evaluates the susceptibility from sine-Gordon form factors, its two-kink and one-breather channels providing a lower bound on the universal amplitude. The Baxter--Johnson--Krinsky--McCoy solution supplies the kink mass for different couplings. Infinite-system density-matrix renormalization group simulations built on these masses reproduce the master formula.
summary: The authors calculate the entanglement asymmetry in the gapped XYZ spin chain by linking it to the static susceptibility via a charged-moment identity. They combine theoretical results from sine-Gordon form factors with numerical iDMRG simulations to derive a universal master formula for this asymmetry. This work provides a rigorous quantitative measure of symmetry breaking encoded in quantum entanglement.
main_problem: The paper aims to measure entanglement asymmetry ($\Delta S_A$) and determine its universal amplitude in a gapped phase of the XYZ spin-$ rac12$ chain where U(1) symmetry is broken.
main_result: They derive a master formula for $\Delta S_A^{(n)}(\ell)$ involving logarithmic growth, providing a lower bound on the universal amplitude $c$ via two-kink and one-breather contributions.
method: The calculation combines a charged-moment identity with a non-conservation sum rule derived from sine-Gordon form factors, which are then validated using infinite-system iDMRG simulations.
model_or_system: The system is the XYZ spin-$ rac12$ chain Hamiltonian in its gapped, U(1)-breaking phase. The analysis utilizes concepts from conformal field theory (sine-Gordon model) and quantum entanglement measures.
key_observables: Entanglement Asymmetry ($\Delta S_A$), Static Susceptibility ($\chi_{zz}$), Kink mass ($M$), Universal amplitude $c( eta^2)$.
important_parameters: Anisotropy parameter $\gamma$, replica index $n$, interval length $\ell$, and the coupling constant related to the sine-Gordon model ($\xi_{sG}$).
main_assumptions: The calculation relies on a charged-moment identity, treating the system in the continuum limit via the sine-Gordon model, and assuming the leading asymptotic behavior of the entanglement entropy.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison between iDMRG results and theoretical bounds for $c( eta^2)$, show the convergence of $\Delta S_A^{(n)}(\ell)$ to a master formula as interval length increases, and plot the rise of $\Delta S_A^{(n)}(\ell)$ with increasing anisotropy $\gamma$.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by establishing the charged-moment identity linking asymmetry to susceptibility. It then evaluates this susceptibility using form factors (sine-Gordon model) to derive a lower bound on the amplitude, which is finally confirmed and refined through iDMRG simulations.
why_interesting: This work provides deep insights into how entanglement measures quantify symmetry breaking in quantum many-body systems, connecting concepts from critical phenomena (CFT/sine-Gordon) with modern tools like entanglement entropy calculations.
